correctness.rationale: PASS: In barycentric blocks n_i=d_i+1, a target Y of total 1+t in each factor decomposes as A+tB with A in k-skeleton iff one can choose positive supports s_i whose sum of costs s_i-1 is at most k and whose largest s_i target coordinates carry at least 1. Their minimum possible sum over target blocks is s_i(1+t)/n_i at the product centroid. Consequently Σceil(n_i/(1+t))≤k+r is sufficient for every target and necessary for the centroid; all t≥0 boundaries are included. The minimum over finitely many support allowances gives the exact rational attained threshold. An independent exact-fraction support-budget enumeration for small products (1,1),(1,2),(2,2),(1,1,1), sample t including 0,1/2,1,2 confirmed the ceiling/centroid criterion. No finite enumeration substitutes for the general capacity argument.
